title: Cheat clients
note: Open-source cheat clients. Identifiers verified against each client's public source (see references).

rules.name: Meteor Client — mod metadata
rules.description: A mod archive declares the mod id "meteor-client", the identifier used by Meteor Client.
rules.falsePositives: Very low. The mod id is declared by the client's own metadata. A third party could reuse the id, which is why the package-structure rule is evaluated independently and both are reported.
rules.limitations: Detects the archive on disk only. It does not prove the client was launched or used on a specific server; correlate with logs, Prefetch and memory findings.

rules.name: Meteor Client — class package structure
rules.description: A Java archive contains compiled classes under the package "meteordevelopment.meteorclient", which belongs to Meteor Client.
rules.falsePositives: Very low. Addons legitimately depend on these packages but do not ship them; a jar that contains the classes contains the client code.
rules.limitations: Renamed/re-obfuscated forks change package names and will not match. Detects presence on disk, not use.

rules.name: Meteor Client — classes loaded in a running JVM
rules.description: The internal class path of Meteor Client was found in the memory of a running Java (Minecraft) process, indicating its classes were loaded.
rules.falsePositives: Low. The string could be present if the user opened the client's jar in a Java-based tool running in the same JVM, which is uncommon for a game process.
rules.limitations: Only examines Java processes running at scan time. If the game was closed before the scan, no memory evidence exists.
